posts.claim: Parliament can extend presidential term limits to seven years without taking the vote to a referendum.
posts.claim_source: Capital FM: Cherargei threatens fresh bid to extend Ruto’s stay in power, 12 Oct 2026
posts.truth: Changing presidential term limits requires a mandatory referendum.
posts.pride: Sovereign power over terms rests with wananchi.
posts.source: Constitution of Kenya 2010, Article 255(1)(f) and Article 256; Elections Act, s.49
proof: Article 255(1)(f) of the Constitution protects presidential terms from direct MP votes.
Any bill altering term limits must pass both houses and go to a citizen ballot.
At least 20 percent of registered voters across 24 counties must vote in the poll.
posts.message: No politician can extend presidential term limits through Parliament alone without a national referendum.
posts.action: Read Article 255 of the Constitution to protect your vote

scripts.radio: Hamjambo msikilizaji. This is Kenyans Are Asking, and this week we look at the fuel pump. On paper, the National Assembly has just approved an extension of fuel tax relief. Lawmakers patted themselves on the back, telling us they are cushioning Kenyans from the rising cost of living. But drive into any petrol station from Mombasa to Kisumu, and the story on the ground is completely different—pump prices have surged once again. So, where is this relief going? If taxes were cushioned or extended, why is that relief not reaching the boda boda rider, the matatu operator, or the family struggling with rising food costs? The hard truth is that our fuel pricing formula remains an opaque black box. Far too often, paper relief gets swallowed up in settling legacy debts with oil marketers or plugging deficits in stabilization funds, while mwananchi absorbs the full shock at the pump. Passing relief in parliament makes for great headlines, but accountability is measured in the shillings leaving your pocket at the till. Until EPRA and the Ministry of Energy lay bare the exact ledger showing who benefits from this tax variance, these extensions remain political theatre. Kwa ufupi: Bunge limeidhinisha kuongezwa kwa unafuu wa kodi ya mafuta, lakini bei vituoni inazidi kupanda. Wananchi wana haki ya kuuliza: ikiwa serikali inatoa unafuu wa kodi, mbona bei ya mafuta haishuki mfukoni mwa mwananchi?
scripts.voice_note: Hey everyone, quick update from Kenyans Are Asking. You might have seen the news that Parliament approved an extension on fuel tax relief this week. It sounds like a win, right? But check your receipt the next time you fuel—pump prices are actually climbing. Here is the disconnect: every time politicians announce 'relief', the actual margin never trickles down to you. Instead, it gets swallowed into backroom settlements with oil marketers or diverted to offset stabilization arrears, while you pay full price. We cannot keep celebrating tax relief that only exists on parliamentary records while our daily transport costs go up. If public money is being used to cushion fuel, that discount must reflect at the pump. Ask your MP: who exactly is this fuel relief protecting, if not the taxpayer?
